mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline correlates with negative 20d SPX returns in >60% of cases or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that boosts corporate profit margins and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE <3.5% fails to produce positive 5d SPX returns in >60% of instances or Rank IC <0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals strong aggregate demand, driving positive equity returns as corporate earnings rise over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise but SPX 20d returns are negative in >60% of cases or interaction term Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS >2.5% and rising), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity drive negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS >2.5% and rising correlates with positive 60d SPX returns in >60% of cases or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1.2 million units (HOUST >1200.0) indicate robust consumer confidence and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST >1200.0 fails to produce positive 5d SPX returns in >60% of instances or Rank IC <0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic growth, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth correlates with negative 20d SPX returns in >60% of cases or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that prompts Fed tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY >3.0% fails to produce negative 60d SPX returns in >60% of cases or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment decline (UNRATE) and payroll growth (PAYEMS) signal rapid labor market tightening, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE decline and PAYEMS growth occur together but SPX 5d returns are negative in >60% of cases or interaction term Rank IC <0.03.
